messages:
nina: Quick architecture sync: we need a clear pin/unpin contract between the runtime and host allocator before we build tiny-slab + coalesce. Current ad-hoc refs are biting us in races.

omar: Agreed. What's the concise contract you want?

nina: Proposal (high level): pin(page_id) -> returns pin_handle; pin_handle must be released via unpin(pin_handle). Pin_handle is an opaque 64-bit token with a generation counter so stale unpins can be detected. Also add try_pin(page_id) that fails fast if page is currently being migrated/evicted.

claire: Generation counter is great. We should also include a pin_mode: READ (shared) vs WRITE (exclusive) so compaction can know when a slot is hot.

ben: Important: fastpath tiny-slab allocations should avoid a heavyweight pin syscall. Maybe the slab pre-pins its backing host pages and exposes a prebound pin_handle per slot; alloc returns that handle without syscall.

omar: That reduces syscalls but complicates eviction. How do we unmap a prebound slab page if it's holding prebound pin_handles?

nina: Eviction lifecycle idea: 1) mark slab as draining (no new allocs), 2) wait for active pin_handles to drop to zero (with a bounded grace period), 3) if still nonzero after timeout, escalate by copying live slots to new slab (compaction) and then unpin old page. We must ensure copy is safe if writers exist.

claire: Writers need a transient write-lock upgrade. Maybe allocate copy-on-write semantics for slab compaction: on copy start, atomically flip slot state to COPYING; writers after that will allocate fresh slot and migrate live data. Readers with old pin_handles can continue until they release.

ben: We need cheap checks on hot path: is_copying bit per slot should be an atomic flag checked only on write path. Reads are unaffected. That keeps alloc/lookup cheap.

omar: About try_pin: it's useful during compaction to avoid blocking. But we must guarantee progress: if try_pin fails because compaction is active, runtime may either queue work or use fallback allocator.

nina: Fallback semantics: if try_pin fails, two options: synchronous fallback to full allocator (may block), or return a short retry hint so caller can coalesce/queue. We should default to retry_hint for microbatch paths and blocking fallback for critical paths.

claire: Telemetry needed: pin_latency_fastpath, pin_latency_slowpath, pin_try_fail_rate, slab_drain_time, slab_compaction_ops, slot_copy_failures. Also record stale_unpin_count when generation mismatch happens.

ben: API sketch for the runtime-client (stringified):
```
// returns {handle, mode}
pin_result = host_alloc.pin(page_id, mode, flags);
// flags: TRY_ONLY | FASTPATH_OK | FORCE_ALLOC
// on success: pin_result.handle -> opaque token
host_alloc.unpin(pin_result.handle);
```

omar: Also add a host_alloc.inspect(handle) for debug that returns slab_id, slot_idx, generation. Only accessible in debug builds or tracing collector.

nina: We must specify ordering and memory barriers: after pin returns, the caller must see the page contents; host must ensure any in-flight DMA completes before returning. Unpin must be visible to compactor within X ms. Let's choose 2ms as target for visible unpin in fastpath.

claire: 2ms target seems tight but reasonable for p99; need kernel-level tuning for DMA completion interrupts and our completion thread scheduling. We'll document expectations and make them configurable.

ben: Security note: pin_handles must be unguessable and validated by host to avoid cross-tenant misuse. Use 64-bit random token + slab-local checksum. Host checks mapping before unpin.

omar: Concern: storing generation and token per pinned slot increases memory per slot. But slots are small; overhead acceptable if we keep metadata packed. We'll benchmark.

nina: Backward compatibility: implement the contract behind a feature flag and keep old API for a grace period. New clients can opt in. We'll add a compatibility shim that translates old pin/unpin semantics into new token handles for legacy code paths.

claire: Implementation risk list: 1) race between copy start and writer; 2) stuck slab when tenant drops but kernel delays unpin; 3) token validation path being hot if not optimized.

ben: Mitigations: 1) atomic COPYING flag + upgrade path for writers; 2) compaction fallback after timeout and a watchdog that force-copies; 3) inline fastpath token validation with small L1-friendly table per-slab.

omar: Testing: unit tests for stale unpin, cross-tenant misuse, copy-on-write correctness. Fuzz unpin/token sequences and add a stress suite that drives concurrent alloc/free under eviction pressure.

nina: Deployment plan: feature-flagged on one staging rack. Metrics: p50/p95 alloc latency, pin_try_fail_rate, slab_drain_time, host_mem_delta. If any signal spikes, rollback flag.

infra-bot: Created EXP-2024-412: "pin-handle contract + tiny-slab tokenized pins" assigned [nina, omar, claire, ben].

nina: I'll write the RFC draft with these API signatures and the compaction state machine. Please comment on the doc by EOD. We'll converge and then implement fastpath alloc PR.

ben: I'll prototype slab metadata layout and a tiny inline token validator.

claire: I'll own the telemetry spec and trace spans.

omar: I'll add unit tests and the fuzz harness.

nina: Thanks team. This contract should make the tiny-slab + coalesce build much safer.
